annotations.title: Is this service covered by the vendor's HIPAA agreement, or FedRAMP authorised?

description: Can I put regulated data in this cloud service? Give a service name and a regime and get what the publisher's own page says, verbatim, with the date. For "hipaa": whether the vendor's own page names that service on its list of services covered by its HIPAA business associate agreement, the vendor's own sentence about what the agreement covers, and the date the vendor last updated that list -- including services a vendor states are NOT covered, which is the answer most often got wrong from memory (OpenAI's own page says web search with live internet access is not HIPAA eligible). For "fedramp": the status, impact level, authorisation date and authorisation type of that vendor's cloud service offering, from the US General Services Administration's own daily marketplace export -- about the OFFERING, because the government's file does not publish which of a vendor's products sit inside an authorisation boundary. Covers Google Cloud, Google SecOps, Google Workspace, Microsoft Azure and OpenAI. AWS is deliberately absent: its site terms forbid automated collection, so its pages are not sources here, and that is a fact about what may be read and not about AWS. This is a lookup of published sentences, not advice: it never says whether a service may lawfully be used for anything, and a service we do not hold comes back "not in our records", never as a no.

regime.description: Which question: "hipaa" for the vendor's business associate agreement coverage, "fedramp" for the government's FedRAMP record of the vendor's offering.

service.description: The service, as near as you have it: "Cloud Run", "BigQuery", "Google Cloud Storage", "Azure Government", "openai web search". Matched against the service names the vendors themselves print; a partial name comes back as a list of candidates rather than a guess.
